blocks.text: [1] [^n2653]And Jesus six days before the passover[^n2654] came to Bethany, where was Lazarus, [2] whom Jesus raised from among the dead. [^n2655]And they made[^n2656] a feast for him there: [3] and Martha was serving; while Lazarus was one of them that sat with him. [^n2657]And [4] at the time of Jesus’ being at Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, [^n2658]great multitudes of the Jews heard that Jesus was there: and they came, not because of Jesus alone, but [Arabic, p. 147] that they might look also on Lazarus, whom he raised from among the dead. [5, 6] [^n2659]And the chief priests considered how they might kill Lazarus also; [^n2660]because [7] many of the Jews were going on his account, and believing in Jesus. [^n2661]And Mary took a case of the ointment of fine nard, of great price, [^n2662]and opened it, and poured [8] it out on the head of Jesus as he was reclining; [^n2663]and she anointed his feet, and wiped them with her hair: and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment. [9, 10] [^n2664]But Judas Iscariot, one of the disciples, he that was to betray him, said, [^n2665]Why was [11] not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given unto the poor? [^n2666]This he said, not because of his care for the poor, but because he was a thief, and the chest [12] was with him, and what was put[^n2667] into it he used to bear. [^n2668]And that displeased the rest of the disciples also within themselves, and they said, Why went this ointment [13] to waste? [^n2669]It was possible that it should be sold for much, and the poor be given [14] it. [^n2670]And they were angry with[^n2671] Mary. [^n2672]And Jesus perceived it, and said unto them, [^n2673]Leave her; why molest ye her? a good work hath she accomplished on me: [^n2674]for the [15] day of my burial kept she it. [^n2675]At all times the poor are with you, and when ye [16] wish ye can do them a kindness: [^n2676]but I am not at all times with you. [^n2677]And for this cause, when she poured[^n2678] this ointment on my body, it is as if she did it for my burial, [17] and anointed my body beforehand. [^n2679]And verily I say unto you, In every place where this my gospel shall be proclaimed in all the world, what she did shall be told for a memorial of her.

[18, 19] [Arabic, p. 148] [^n2680]And when Jesus said that, he went out leisurely to go to Jerusalem. [^n2681]And when he arrived at Bethphage and at Bethany, beside the mount which is [20] called the mount of Olives, [^n2682]Jesus sent two of his disciples, and he said unto them, Go [21] into this village that is opposite you: [^n2683]and when ye enter it, ye shall find an ass tied, and [22] a colt with him,[^n2684] which no man ever yet mounted: loose him, and bring them[^n2685] unto me. [^n2686]And if any man say unto you, Why loose ye them? say unto him thus, We [23] seek them for our Lord; and straightway send them hither. [^n2687]All this was, that what was said in the prophet might be fulfilled, which said,
[24] [^n2688]Say ye unto the daughter of Zion,
Behold, thy King cometh unto thee,
Meek, and riding upon an ass,
And upon a colt the foal of an ass.

[25] [^n2689]And the disciples did not know this at that time: but after that Jesus was glorified, his disciples remembered that these things were written of him, and that this [26] they had done unto him. [^n2690]And when the two disciples went, they found as he had [27] said unto them, and they did as Jesus charged them. [^n2691]And when they loosed them, [28] their owners said unto them, Why loose ye them? [^n2692]They said unto them, We seek [29] them for our Lord. [^n2693]And they let them go. And they brought the ass and the colt, [30] and they placed on the colt their garments; and Jesus mounted it. [^n2694]And most of the multitudes spread their garments on the ground before him: and others cut branches [31] from the trees, and threw them in the way. [^n2695]And when he neared his[^n2696] descent from [Arabic, p. 149] the mount of Olives, all the disciples began to rejoice and to praise God with [32] a loud voice for all the powers which they had seen; [^n2697]and they said, Praise in the highest; Praise to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name [33] of the Lord; [^n2698]and blessed[^n2699] is the kingdom that cometh, that of[^n2700] our father David: [^n2701]Peace in heaven, and praise in the highest.

[34] [^n2702]And a great multitude, that which came to the feast, when they heard that Jesus [35] was coming to Jerusalem, took young palm branches,[^n2703] [^n2704]and went forth to meet him, and cried and said, Praise: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord, the [36] King of Israel. [^n2705]Certain therefore of the Pharisees from among the multitudes [37] said unto him, Our Master, rebuke thy disciples. [^n2706]He said unto them, Verily I say unto you, If these were silent, the stones would cry out.

[38, 39] [^n2707]And when he drew near, and saw the city, he wept over it, and said, [^n2708]Would that thou hadst known the things that are[^n2709] for thy peace, in this thy day! now that is [40] hidden from thine eyes. [^n2710]There shall come unto thee days when thine enemies [41] shall encompass thee, and straiten thee from every quarter, [^n2711]and shall get possession of[^n2712] thee, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee a stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.

[42] [^n2713]And when he entered into Jerusalem, the whole city was agitated, and they said, [43] Who is this? [^n2714]And the multitudes said, This is Jesus, the prophet that is from Nazareth [44] of Galilee. [^n2715]And the multitude which was with him bare witness that he called [45] Lazarus from the grave, and raised him from among the dead. [^n2716]And for this cause great multitudes went out to meet him, because they heard the sign which he did.

n2656.text: Lit. he made (cf. first note to § 38, 43, last sentence).

n2700.text: The Arabic has to, but it probably represents the Syriac text with the meaning given above.

n2703.text: Lit. the heart (or, pith) of the palm. The word pith, which occurs also in the Æhiopic version (Ezek. xxvii. 25; Jubilees, ch. 16) and in Ibn-at-Tayyib’s exposition, though not in the Brit. Mus. gospel text, is perhaps used here of the inner branches from its resemblance to the post-biblical Hebrew word employed in accounts of the Feast of Tabernacles.

n2709.text: Lit. are found, a rendering due to the Syriac.

n2712.text: So Ciasca’s text, following Vat. ms. The other ms. has drag, which by restoring a diacritical point to the third radical would give destroy, the reading of the Syriac versions. Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary has hide.
